workflows.title: WF4 Data exfiltration
workflows.description: Size an outbound transfer, name the data, find where it came from, and confirm who sent it.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead D, or WF1/WF2 showed large uploads.  
**You need:** the user name.  
**Goal:** decide whether intellectual property left the company and how much. About 5 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

steps.title: How much left, and to where?

evidence.title: Total to file sharing
evidence.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range]))

evidence.title: Upload volume by destination
evidence.expr: sum by (url_domain) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__interval]))

card.look: upload volume over time per destination.
card.bad: over 100 MB to a personal file-sharing or paste site, especially a run of near-identical chunks.
card.if_bad: block the destination at the proxy for everyone, then Step 2.
card.if_clean: uploads go to the corporate SharePoint or a sanctioned SaaS. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Uploaded files
evidence.expr: topk(50, sum by (url_domain, file_name) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | file_name!="" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])))

card.bad: archives split into numbered parts (`.7z.001`), program or vehicle platform names, CAD or battery data.
card.if_bad: send the file names to the data owner (engineering) to confirm sensitivity.
card.if_clean: personal files or nothing named. Check Step 3 before closing.

steps.title: Where did the files come from?

evidence.title: Shares opened by this user
evidence.expr: sum by (share, relative_target) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | user="$user" | event_id="5145" [$__range]))

card.bad: an engineering share the user does not normally use, opened just before the uploads.
card.if_bad: the share owner needs to know. Add the share to the case.
card.if_clean: no share access. The data may have been local.

evidence.title: VPN sessions for this user
evidence.expr: sum by (event, src_ip, src_country, hip_compliant) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" [$__range]))

card.look: how the user was connected while the uploads happened.
card.bad: VPN from abroad, a failed device posture check, or a sign-in workflow (WF1) that came back compromised.
card.if_bad: treat it as an attacker, not an insider. Run [[WF1 for this user]].
card.if_clean: on-site or normal VPN. Insider risk: involve HR and legal before contacting the user.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Confirmed exfiltration** if Step 1 was red and Step 2 or Step 3 names sensitive data.

**Do these now:**
1. Block the destination domain at the proxy for all users.
2. Notify the data owner with the file names and the total from Step 1.
3. If Step 4 says attacker: legal and privacy start the IP-theft process. If insider: HR and legal before anyone talks to the user.

**Then go to:**
- [[WF1 for this user]]
- [[Case timeline]]

also.say: Session was not the user. Treat as attacker, run WF1.
